notes: Record's own Contacts: a single GeneralContact pointing to spase://SMWG/Person/UNKNOWN — non-qualifying and not a real person; yields no candidate.

GOES-18 has NO Instrument records in SPASE. The registry path /SMWG/Instrument/GOES/ lists subdirectories 1-17 only; GOES/16 and GOES/17 register only MAG + Ephemeris. All four space-weather instruments (EXIS, SUVI, SEISS, MAG) are therefore missing from SPASE and were pursued via provider pages and description papers. This is a significant metadata gap for curators (see instrument_coverage and pending_instrument_runs).

No NASA-HQ CMAD exists — GOES-R is NOAA-funded (expected=false). GOES-R analog documents are the Product Definition and Users' Guide (PUG) and NCEI instrument calibration reports; these were not treated as CMAD-strength evidence.

SUVI description paper (Darnel et al. 2022, 10.1029/2022SW003044): selection CONFIDENT — title names the instrument, 16 authors, Space Weather journal, timing (2022) aligns with the GOES-16/17/18 series operations. Backward alphabetization scan: no sorted suffix of >=5 (positions 11-16 are the unsorted Lockheed Martin build team). Not alphabetized; positions 1-3 (Darnel, Seaton, Bethge) taken Strong; 4-16 excluded as SUVI instrument-team depth.

MAG description paper (Loto'aniu et al. 2019, 10.1007/s11214-019-0600-3): selection CONFIDENT — 'The GOES-16 Spacecraft Science Magnetometer' describes the GOES-R series magnetometer flown identically on GOES-18, 15 authors, Space Science Reviews, 2019 (series operations era). Not alphabetized; positions 1-3 (Loto'aniu, Redmon, Califf) Strong; 4-15 excluded as depth. Position-4 author Howard J. Singer is independently included at Medium via the GOES-16 MAG SPASE record's PrincipalInvestigator role and the instrument Acknowledgement — the symmetric rule at work (independent source, not paper position 4, is what includes him).

SEISS overview paper (Galica et al. 2016, 10.1117/12.2228537): selection CONFIDENT — title 'GOES-R Space Environment In-Situ Suite: instruments overview...', SPIE, 6 authors, 2016 (pre-launch design/overview, valid per the fuzzy lower boundary). Not alphabetized; positions 1-3 (Galica, Dichter, Tsui, Assurance Technology Corporation) Strong; 4-6 excluded as depth.

EXIS description-paper selection UNCERTAIN and downgraded one tier: EXIS is a two-instrument suite (EUVS + XRS) with no single peer-reviewed overview paper. Used the EUVS design paper (Eparvier et al. 2009, 10.1117/12.826445) and the XRS design/calibration paper (Woods et al. 2024, 10.1029/2024JA032925) as component description papers; their positions 1-3 taken at Medium (would be Strong absent the uncertainty). Francis G. Eparvier is retained at Strong via an independent provider source: NOAA SWPC presentations name him PI of both EUVS and XRS. EXIS recorded in pending_instrument_runs for a dedicated per-component run.

GOES-18 is a NOAA weather platform; no space-weather-focused mission-overview *paper* was identified. The GOES-R Series book (Goodman, Schmit, Daniels, Redmon, eds.) is Earth-science program-level and was not used to mint mission-overview candidates; Redmon already enters via the MAG description paper. No observatory-level mission-overview positions 4-5 were harvested for this reason.
ABI and GLM (Earth-pointing weather instruments) are part of the physical observatory but outside heliophysics authorship scope; noted in instrument_coverage, not pursued.

Initials-only names (G. E. Galica, B. K. Dichter, S. Tsui, W. Rowland, etc.) are recorded as printed in the SPIE/SSR author lists; downstream should expand and disambiguate. Alison Jarvis and F. J. Rich each appear across two instrument contexts — flagged inline.
